title: Chapter 95
content:
The thrill of the date was short-lived. Kang Il-hyun’s roadster had been drifting further and further off the beaten path for a while now, eventually trading the sleek downtown asphalt for the narrow, winding alleys of a typical mountainside daldongne—a neglected hillside shantytown. The road soon narrowed to a crawl, forcing them to park halfway up and walk the rest of the way.

Stepping out into the humid air, Jakyeong froze at the sight of a dilapidated little sundry shop tucked against the corner of the lane.

Sitting on a weathered wooden deck outside the crumbling storefront was a frail, white-haired grandmother with a deep mole resting beside her eye, methodically peeling cloves of garlic. She glanced up at the sound of unfamiliar footsteps.

The sight of the distinct facial mark made Jakyeong instinctively take a half-step back.

"Need something, travelers?"

Her voice was pitched high, struggling against failing hearing.

Instantly, the landscape of Jakyeong's memory rewrote itself. Back then, starvation had been a chronic, grinding state of being. Driven past the edge of endurance, he used to sneak down to this very shop to swipe a stale loaf of bread. On the occasions he got caught, the shopkeeper would beat him black and blue—until the old woman, the owner's mother, would step out, shielding the bruised boy in her skirts and quietly slipping a heel of bread or a carton of milk into his hands.

And she, too, had worn that exact, prominent mole beside her eye.

Warmth brushed against Jakyeong’s back. A heavy hand rested over his shoulder. Turning around, he found Il-hyun’s dark eyes locked onto his face.

"Here..."

"How did you know about this place?" Jakyeong breathed.

"There are very few things in this world I cannot find when I look."

Jakyeong fell silent, his gaze sweeping over the neighborhood once more. The steep concrete steps where he used to run drug drops, the narrow crawlspaces where he hid to escape his parents' fists—everything remained frozen in time. As he hesitated, rooted to the spot, Il-hyun extended an open hand.

"Want to go see the house where you grew up?"

"..."

"Tell me if it's too much. We can turn back right now."

Jakyeong stayed mute. The second he fled South Korea, he had sworn never to set foot in this district again. Yet as the years passed and survival became a baseline, a morbid, lingering curiosity had taken root. How had it aged? Did the house still exist? If he had wanted to track it down, he certainly had the resources—he simply hadn't possessed the stomach for it.

Yet standing here now, the dread felt remarkably weightless.

While Jakyeong drifted in his thoughts, Il-hyun slipped into the sundry shop, reemerging a moment later unwrapping two cheap popsicles. The muffled sound of a card reader chiming and an old man grumbling echoed from inside. Il-hyun handed one of the treats across, already sinking his own teeth into the strawberry ice.

Watching Kang Il-hyun consume a cheap, thousand-won popsicle on a broken curb was a sight roughly as surreal as watching Wang Han grow a full head of thick, flowing hair.

With the cold treat resting between his lips, Il-hyun offered a gentle, inquiring hum. "Ready to walk up?"

He held out his hand. Jakyeong stared at the palm for a long beat before stepping past him. Il-hyun caught up instantly, sliding his fingers into Jakyeong's. When Jakyeong tried to pull away—finding the sight of two grown men holding hands on a public hill absurd—Il-hyun simply laced their fingers tighter, firmly interlocking them as they climbed the incline.

Faded red spray-paint graffiti stained the concrete retaining walls on either side of the alley, and elderly residents sat resting on low plastic stools outside their doorways. As they pushed up the punishing grade, the heat finally caught up to Il-hyun; shedding his tailored suit jacket, he draped it over his forearm and rolled his cuffs up to his elbows.

The flight of concrete steps where a drunk once tumbled and broke his neck; the rusted tin roof of Mr. Wang’s house—every landmark remained nailed to its original coordinates. The deeper the memories dug, the tighter the pressure grew behind Jakyeong's ribs. Whether from the physical exertion or the psychological ghosts, his boots felt heavier with every yard.

As they drew closer to the dilapidated gate, his throat constricted so violently he could no longer force his feet forward.

His palms slicked with cold sweat. He tore his hand from the interlock, frantically rubbing his damp fingers against the denim of his trousers.

"Want to turn around?"

Jakyeong gave a slow, mechanical shake of his head. Since they had already dragged themselves this far, he needed to see it through.

Standing before the securely latched blue iron gate, Jakyeong drew a long, rattling breath.

The second he pushed past this threshold, phantom hands wrenched his hair backward, and heavy boots ground his face into the dirt.

His dead mother would emerge with the demonic, rabid snarl of a beast, raking long fingernails across his skin. His monstrous father would roar obscenities, bringing a heavy wooden club down across his spine.

His legs refused to obey. Only after a grueling struggle of will did he finally force his trembling fingers to touch the cold metal of the gate.

The surface bit into his skin with an icy shiver. Slowly, he pushed.

Kreeeeak—

As the rusted hinges groaned and he crossed the threshold, Jakyeong froze dead in his tracks.

The front courtyard was an explosion of vibrant, blooming flora. Every square inch of earth had been meticulously cultivated, weeded, and tended with obsessive care. The structure itself had been thoroughly scrubbed, repaired, and painted—transformed from a ruin into a cozy, rustic cottage.

Jakyeong grabbed Il-hyun’s forearm, hauling him back.

"We need to leave... Someone's living here."

Il-hyun didn't even blink. He walked over to the wooden porch, dropped heavily onto the planks, and pulled a fresh pack of cigarettes from his pocket. Striking a match, he took a slow drag, then patted the weathered wood beside him, gesturing for Jakyeong to sit.

Looking around the perimeter in disbelief, Jakyeong stepped cautiously through the gate.

"There has to be an owner..."

"There isn't."

No matter how he looked at it, the property screamed domestic care. Without daily upkeep, it couldn't possibly look this pristine. It bore zero resemblance to the nightmare bunker of his youth.

Noticing the climbing ivy along the perimeter wall, Jakyeong realized the entire surface was choked with thick, blooming red roses.

He sat down on the edge of the porch with agonizing care. Il-hyun slid closer, slipping a fresh cigarette between Jakyeong’s lips and sparking the tip.

Then, without ceremony, the corporate heir kept his oxfords on, swung his legs up onto the wooden deck, and laid his head straight down into Jakyeong’s lap.

"Ah... This is paradise."

Jakyeong exhaled a long ribbon of smoke, his eyes wandering across the transformed yard. It felt deeply unsettling—as if the house belonged to an entirely different dimension.

Because it sat perched at the very summit of the hill, a cool, refreshing breeze swept down across the porch, cutting through the summer humidity and evaporating the sweat from his brow.

Scanning the courtyard, Jakyeong's gaze finally snagged on the back door.

The heavy wooden panel remained firmly shut. Yet as he stared, his mind played back the phantom audio of his mother entertaining strange, abusive men behind that very barrier.

He swallowed hard, dropping his eyes down to the man resting in his lap.

Il-hyun lay completely motionless, his eyes closed.

"Are you sleeping?"

"No."

"How... how did you find this place?"

Il-hyun opened his eyes. Within the warm, lazy irises, Jakyeong’s face was reflected in sharp detail.

"While I was hunting you down last year. Stumbled on it by pure coincidence."

Last year... Staring at the vibrant flowerbeds and painted roses draping the walls, a sudden, heavy realization bloomed in Jakyeong's chest.

Il-hyun pushed himself up, shifting into a sitting position to meet Jakyeong's gaze with unusual, solemn gravity.

"I came by shortly after you fled. The place was rotting—abandoned, layered in dust. The locals whispered it was haunted, so no one dared touch it."

"..."

"I wanted to see what you looked like when you were small."

Il-hyun trailed off, his mind flashing back to his initial inspection of the hovel: broken furniture scattered across rotting floorboards; a thorough search that yielded nothing but discarded adult novelties, drug baggies, empty soju bottles, and hanafuda cards.

"Not a single trace, nor a single object indicating a child had ever lived here. I honestly thought I had tracked down the wrong address."

Jakyeong bit down hard on his lower lip. Of course there weren't any traces. There was never anything worth keeping.

"Fuck," Il-hyun muttered, grinding his teeth. "At least if you bring a child into this world, the bare minimum requirement is a single photograph. Is that really so much to ask?"

The only garments left behind had been threadbare rags—not aged into tatters from time, but born into wretched decay. Toys, notebooks, or writing utensils had been entirely absent from the inventory.

A dark, lethal venom crept into Il-hyun’s eyes.

Hearing the man stand up for him—directing his fury at the ghosts of his abusers—sent a sharp, burning pinch straight to the bridge of Jakyeong's nose.

Muttering that it was all ancient history, Jakyeong looked away, but Il-hyun pushed himself up and wandered down into the garden.

Figuring the man needed to burn off his frustration, Jakyeong watched as Il-hyun stepped straight into the immaculate flowerbeds—and began ruthlessly snapping the stems of the blooming roses, one by one, tossing them carelessly to the dirt.

Jakyeong’s brow pinched.

"What are you doing to the flowers?"

Il-hyun offered no verbal reply, continuing his systematic vandalism until he had gathered a chaotic, jagged armful of multi-colored blossoms. He turned, marching straight across the courtyard.

With his shirt partially unbuttoned, a cigarette dangling from his lip, and a violently mangled bouquet clutched in his fist, he bore an uncanny resemblance to the unhinged villain of an action thriller.

He looked ready to pull a concealed pistol and open fire.

Instead, he dropped the crushed flowers directly into Jakyeong’s lap.

Extinguishing his cigarette against the deck with the heel of his shoe, Il-hyun beamed with radiant satisfaction.

"A formal offering to comfort the unloved child you used to be."

Ah... What on earth am I supposed to do with this man?

Taking a deep breath, the heavy air brought back the phantom sensory profile of that era: cheap liquor, heavy perfume, stale tobacco, the metallic reek of fresh semen, and the iron tang of blood. Combined with the venomous screams of parents howling that he should never have been born.

Jakyeong kept his eyes pinned to the wooden planks, unable to lift his chin. His nose burned, and his vision swam with unbidden heat.

"Darling. Are you going to take them before my arms fall off?"

Stung by the teasing quip, Jakyeong looked up.

In place of the monsters who had tormented his childhood stood a breathtakingly handsome man, offering a crushed bouquet with an endearing, brilliant smile. The rich floral perfume was thick enough to make his head spin.

Without thinking, he accepted the bundle.

The moment his hands were full, Il-hyun pulled out his phone and slid onto the bench directly beside him, wrapping an arm around his shoulders.

Before Jakyeong could protest, the camera app opened.

The preview window captured their reflections side by side against the rustic wooden backdrop. Jakyeong looked profoundly stiff and awkward.

"What are you doing?"

"Commemorating the occasion."

Panic flared. Jakyeong instinctively tried to scramble away, but a heavy arm hauled him back, forcing the shot.

The resulting capture was an absolute disaster: Jakyeong looking like a deer caught in high-beam headlights while clutching a pile of violently murdered flowers, contrasted against Il-hyun grinning like a Cheshire cat.

Il-hyun frowned down at the thumbnail.

"Fucking hell. It looks like I'm the only one head-over-heels in love here."

The childish pout coaxed an involuntary snort of laughter out of Jakyeong.

The moment the sound escaped, Il-hyun’s gaze snapped up. Before Jakyeong could blink, fingers caught the back of his neck, wrenching him forward to capture his lips in a bruising, thorough kiss.

The invasion parted his teeth, their tongues tangling in a slow, heated dance before parting.

Following the kiss, Il-hyun pulled him into a crushing embrace, his heavy palm stroking the back of Jakyeong’s head with infinite, rhythmic care.

"Thank you for growing up."

The words hit the back of Jakyeong’s throat like a physical blow.

That was a benediction meant for parents to speak.

Jakyeong buried his face deep into the crook of Il-hyun’s shoulder. He couldn't let the tears fall—if he started here, he would never stop.

"From now on, every ounce of love you were starved of... I will give it all back to you."

The quiet, low vow was devastatingly tender.

It would have been an absolute, peerless memory to carry to the grave—had the man not added a single, fatal postscript:

"And if you ever dare accept love from anyone else..."

Il-hyun paused. Jakyeong held his breath.

"We'll both be buried right here beneath this flowerbed. Understood?"

Jakyeong yanked his head back, glaring up through murderous slits.

Il-hyun simply pressed Jakyeong’s face back down against his shoulder, resuming the gentle, soothing patter along his spine. There, there. Good boy. You're safe.

Was it a confession of undying devotion, or a premeditated terror threat?

To this day, Jakyeong still hadn't figured out the correct answer.
